result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.trav_in_edge()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Traverse from selected nodes to inbound edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L17053-L17096){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.trav_in_edge() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Traverse to inbound edges](/assets/graphs/trav-in-edge.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: in a seven-node directed graph, node C is selected (accent). Right: after trav_in_edge() the node selection is gone and the two edges pointing into C, A to C and E to C, are selected instead (accent)." width="100%"} From the currently selected nodes, moves to all edges where the selected nodes are targets (inbound edges). The current node selection is cleared and replaced with an edge selection. For directed graphs, selects edges where to=selected_node. For undirected graphs, selects all edges incident to selected nodes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The mirror image of `trav_out_edge()`: traversing from "C" to its inbound edges selects both edges pointing into it: ::: {#0d5cf26c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) graph.add_edges([("A", "C"), ("B", "C")]) node_c_id = graph.get_id_from_label("C") graph.select_nodes_by_id([node_c_id]).trav_in_edge() len(graph.get_selected_edge_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
